fullData.title: Adding Decimals on a Number Line
fullData.subject: Arithmetic

problem.statement: Leo walks $0.4$ miles to the park, and then walks another $0.3$ miles to the library. Use the number line to show his total distance and find the sum of $0.4 + 0.3$.

fullData.solutionStrategy: Start at zero and hop forward along the tenths tick marks to find the final landing point.

content.altText: A number line from 0 to 1 divided into tenths, showing a jump from 0 to 0.4.

annotations.steps: Start at zero and make a forward jump of four tenths to reach 0.4.
annotations.strategy: I start at zero because it is our safe home base before taking any steps.
annotations.misconceptions: Start at the given number. Count the moves after it, not the starting mark.
annotations.connections: This connects whole number counting to decimals by using equal jumps on a number line.
annotations.narrative: Start at the point labeled $0$ and move forward $4$ tenths to reach the park at $0.4$.

content.altText: A number line from 0 to 1 with a jump of 0.3 starting from 0.4 and landing at 0.7.

annotations.steps: I start at 0.4 and jump forward three tenths to land on 0.7.
annotations.strategy: I notice that adding decimals is just like adding whole numbers by moving forward on the number line.
annotations.misconceptions: Start at the given number. Count the moves after it, not the starting mark.
annotations.connections: This connects decimal addition to standard linear measurement and length models used with whole numbers.
annotations.narrative: From $0.4$, jump forward $3$ more tenths to land on the library at $0.7$. Therefore, Leo's total distance is $0.7$ miles, giving $0.4 + 0.3 = 0.7$.

challenge.prompt: Leo starts at $0.4$ and hops forward to add $0.3$. After taking his first forward hop of one tenth ($0.1$), which number does he land on?
challenge.rationale: Starting at $0.4$ and hopping forward one tenth lands on $0.5$, because counting on a number line measures the jumps between marks rather than counting the starting tick mark $0.4$.

solverDebug.problemEcho: Leo walks $0.4$ miles to the park, and then walks another $0.3$ miles to the library. Use the number line to show his total distance and find the sum of $0.4 + 0.3$.
solverDebug.body:
Start at the point labeled $0$ and move forward $4$ tenths to reach the park at $0.4$.
---
From $0.4$, jump forward $3$ more tenths to land on the library at $0.7$. Therefore, Leo's total distance is $0.7$ miles, giving $0.4 + 0.3 = 0.7$.

specs.title: Plot the first distance
specs.pedagogicalGoal: Visualize the first addend as a forward jump from zero along a tenths number line.
specs.seedNotes: Draw a number line partitioned into tenths from 0 to 1, showing an initial jump of 4 tenths from 0 to land at 0.4.

specs.title: Add the second distance
specs.pedagogicalGoal: Show that adding decimals corresponds to continuing forward along the number line to determine the total sum.
specs.seedNotes: Add a second jump of 3 tenths (+0.3) starting from 0.4 to land at 0.7, establishing 0.4 + 0.3 = 0.7.
